# An arbitrary asymmetric finite ear on a centroided triangle

This note proves the ordinary cubic cap/section inequality for a complete two-parameter family of actual quadrilaterals. The ear may have arbitrary positive height and arbitrary asymmetry. This is a finite result, rather than a first-variation result. It extends the previously proved symmetric-ear family in `candidate 11020364891cd885` in this centroided subcase. It does not prove the inequality for arbitrary quadrilaterals, or for ears on all cubic-tight triangles.

## 1. Statement and actual geometry

Let

    P1=(2,-1), P2=(-1,2), P3=(-1,-1),
    Q=(X,Y),             X,Y>=0, X+Y>1,
    K=conv{P3,P1,Q,P2}.

Use the three closed caps through the origin with balanced normals

    v1=(1,0), v2=(0,1), v3=(-1,-1).

Write `k=area(K)`, `Q_i=area(K intersect {v_i.x>=0})`, and

    sigma_i=length(K intersect {v_i.x=0})/||v_i||,
    M=sum_i Q_i/sigma_i,
    f_i=2 sqrt(k Q_i)/(sigma_i M).

Then

    f1^2+f2^2+f3^2+f1 f2 f3 < 4.                   (1)

In particular the symmetric zero-diagonal matrix with off-diagonal entries `f_i/2` has largest eigenvalue strictly below one. The source is the original triangle's centroid, namely the origin; it is not asserted to be the quadrilateral's centroid or deepest point.

Set

    r=X+Y-1>0,              p=XY>=0.                (2)

The consecutive turn determinants of the displayed polygon are

    3(Y+1), 3r, 3(X+1), 9.

Its oriented edge-to-origin determinants are

    3, X+2Y, 2X+Y, 3.

Thus the polygon is strictly convex and the origin is strictly interior, including when one of `X,Y` is zero. The three old vertices lie in their three distinct open unique-capture sectors. When `X,Y>0`, the new tip lies in the open double-capture sector of caps 1 and 2. The cases `X=0` or `Y=0` are its actual ray-boundary seams.

Shoelace and direct clipping give

    k=3(r+3)/2,
    sigma1=2+r/(X+1), sigma2=2+r/(Y+1), sigma3=2,
    Q1=(3r+6-sigma1)/2,
    Q2=(3r+6-sigma2)/2,
    Q3=2.                                           (3)

For example the first cut runs from `(0,-1)` to
`(0,(2X+Y)/(X+1))`. Its negative-side quadrilateral has parallel vertical sides of lengths `3` and `sigma1`, at horizontal distance one, so has area `(3+sigma1)/2`. Subtracting from `k` proves the formula for `Q1`. The second formula follows by reflection. The third captured triangle has vertices `P3,(1,-1),(-1,1)`, so its area and normalized section length are both two. These arguments also work when the new tip is on one cut; a cut line has zero planar area.

## 2. A radical-free critical-level test

Put

    T=sum_i Q_i/sigma_i^2,
    U=product_i (Q_i/sigma_i^2),
    E=M^2-kT,
    R=M^2 E^2-4k^3 U.                               (4)

Every omitted geometric quantity is strictly positive. Consequently (1) is equivalent to

    E>0 and R>0.                                    (5)

Indeed, the left side of (1) is

    4kT/M^2 + 8k^(3/2) sqrt(U)/M^3.

Its being less than four is exactly `ME>2k^(3/2)sqrt(U)`, whose squaring is legitimate precisely with `E>0`. This keeps the necessary radical-branch sign; positivity of `R` alone is not enough.

## 3. Reduction retaining the actual two-parameter geometry

Define

    c=3(r+2)/2,    D=4p+3r^2+10r+8,
    h=(4p+r^2+7r+8)/D,    q=(p+r+2)/D.             (6)

To see their geometric meaning, put `a=1/sigma1`, `b=1/sigma2`. Since `(X+1)(Y+1)=p+r+2` and `(X+1)+(Y+1)=r+3`, direct addition gives

    a+b=h,       ab=q.

The cap formulas (3) therefore imply the particularly short exact identities

    M=c h,
    T=c(h^2-2q)-h/2+1/2,
    U=q(c^2 q-c h/2+1/4)/2.                         (7)

In the first identity the constants cancel: `Q1/sigma1=c a-1/2`, `Q2/sigma2=c b-1/2`, and `Q3/sigma3=1`. Thus (7) comes from the same actual quadrilateral; no independent cap or section variables are being substituted.

The actual parameters also satisfy `4p<=(r+1)^2`. We will not need this additional relation: the following algebra is positive on the entire larger quadrant `r>0,p>=0`.

## 4. Explicit positive polynomial certificate

Substituting (6)--(7) into (4) gives

    E=3 E0(r,p)/(4D^2),
    R=27r R0(r,p)/(64D^6),                          (8)

where

    E0=(r+2)(9r^4+73r^3+198r^2+228r+96)
       +2p(9r^4+71r^3+186r^2+210r+96)
       +24p^2(r+1)(r+2).                            (9)

For a concise complete specification of the larger polynomial, write

    R0=sum_{j=0}^6 A_j(r) p^j.                      (10)

Its seven coefficient polynomials have the following factorizations. All coefficient lists are in ascending degree in `r`:

    A0=(r+2)^4 P0(r),
    A1=12(r+2)^3 P1(r),
    A2=12(r+2)^2 P2(r),
    A3=32(r+2)^2 P3(r),
    A4=192(r+2)^2 P4(r),
    A5=1536(r+2)^2 P5(r),
    A6=1024(3r^2+11r+9)(9r^3+54r^2+109r+72).

```text
P0 = [663552, 3778560, 9625088, 14460848, 14226512, 9622452,
4572636, 1532931, 358116, 56190, 5400, 243]
P1 = [497664, 2774016, 6909568, 10127784, 9680204, 6316694,
2863620, 900238, 192369, 26711, 2187, 81]
P2 = [1658880, 8773632, 20708992, 28704164, 25850592, 15799832,
6646108, 1910496, 364947, 43735, 2925, 81]
P3 = [518400, 2300544, 4474696, 4983734, 3481338, 1570257,
453723, 80373, 7875, 324]
P4 = [38880, 138168, 208516, 171635, 82370, 22801, 3336, 198]
P5 = [1134, 3006, 3157, 1610, 393, 36]
```

Equations (8)--(10) are polynomial identities obtained by multiplying the rational expressions (6)--(7) by the displayed denominators. They can be checked by ordinary expansion; the companion exact verifier reconstructs every printed list, rather than substituting numerical samples. Every coefficient is strictly positive. Hence `D>0,E0>0,R0>0` for `r>0,p>=0`. Formula (8) proves (5), and completes the proof of (1).

At `r=0`, the tip lies on the original edge whenever the geometric parameters remain admissible. The original triangle is unchanged, `f1=f2=f3=1`, and equality holds. Thus the explicit factor `r` tracks the actual disappearance of the ear, while the proof is strict for every nonzero ear, including arbitrary asymmetry and arbitrarily large height.

## 5. Affine and actual-diagonal interpretations

The assertion transports under every invertible affine map applied to the entire body, source, and three cut lines. After translating the source, if the linear part is `L`, areas and all the normalized section quantities scale by `|det L|` when normals are transported by `L^(-T)`. Thus `M` and the three `f_i` are unchanged. This is an ordinary-body result only; no non-lattice-preserving map is being applied to a mixed-integer problem.

Consequently the theorem applies to an arbitrary triangle, its centroid, its three centroid cuts parallel to opposite edges, and one actual added tip in any double-capture sector across the corresponding edge. It does not cover arbitrary source positions or arbitrary balanced normals on that triangle.

It also certifies complete strict-incidence portions of actual diagonal motions. For fixed `a,b>0`, let the tip move on the line from the opposite vertex,

    Q(t)=P3+t(a,b)=(ta-1,tb-1).

Every parameter satisfying

    t>max{1/a,1/b,3/(a+b)}

lies in the family above. Throughout that whole interval the spectral level remains strictly below one. This is a critical-level statement and does not assert spectral quasiconvexity below that level.

## 6. Extension to both unique-tip incidence branches

In fact the same conclusion holds throughout the larger actual family

    X,Y>-1,             X+Y>1.                     (11)

These are exactly the strict turn conditions for the displayed quadrilateral. The source remains interior: if, for example, `X<0`, then `Y>1-X`, so `X+2Y>2-X>0` and `2X+Y>X+1>0`. The cases with both coordinates nonnegative were proved above. Since their sum exceeds one, at most one coordinate is negative. Reflection interchanges the two remaining cases, so it is enough to put

    X=-a, Y=r+1+a,       0<=a<1, r>0.              (12)

Here the new tip is uniquely captured by cap 2 when `a>0`. The first cap becomes a triangle rather than a quadrilateral. Its exact data are

    V=r+a+2,     W=3r+2a+4,     k=3(r+3)/2,
    sigma1=2V/(a+2),       Q1=sigma1,
    sigma2=W/V,           Q2=(3r+6-sigma2)/2,
    sigma3=2,             Q3=2.                    (13)

For cap 1, its cut meets `P1Q` and `P3P1`; the base length is `sigma1` and the horizontal height of `P1` is two, so its area equals `sigma1`. The other two calculations are unchanged. At `a=0` the formulas coincide with the actual ray-seam values from (3).

Using (4) and these actual data gives

    E=3 E1(r,a)/(4 V W^2),
    R=27r R1(r,a)/(64 V^2 W^6),                    (14)

where

    E1=12(a+2)^3 +3(a+2)^2(a+19)r
       +3(a+2)(4a+33)r^2 +(17a+73)r^3 +9r^4.     (15)

For the remaining certificate write `R1=sum_{j=0}^{11} B_j(a) r^j`. The complete coefficient factorizations are

    B0=5184(1-a)(a+2)^7,
    B1=288(a+2)^6 [205-182a-17a^2],
    B2=16(a+2)^5 [18799-14241a-3057a^2-97a^3],
    B3=(a+2)^4 [903803-546492a-211566a^2-14684a^3-165a^4],
    B4=2(a+2)^3 [889157-376278a-257322a^2-29756a^3-729a^4],
    B5=3(a+2)^2 [801871-164870a-253382a^2-44598a^3-1809a^4],
    B6=6(a+2) [381053+21565a-112186a^2-29895a^3-1823a^4],
    B7=3 [510977+189486a-100415a^2-46894a^3-4217a^4],
    B8=6 [59686+14249a-6352a^2-1325a^3],
    B9=6 [9365+1403a-319a^2],
    B10=216(2a+25),
    B11=243.                                       (16)

These again are exact polynomial identities. On `0<=a<=1`, the nine bracketed expressions in `B1,...,B9` have the respective positive lower bounds

    6, 1404, 130896, 225072, 337212,
    237149, 359451, 52009, 9046.                    (17)

For the first five brackets, replace each negative power of `a` by one. For the last four, also discard the nonnegative linear term. Thus (17) is elementary and uniform, without polynomial root estimates. All `B_j` are positive for `a<1`, and for `a=1` only `B0` may vanish. In particular `E>0,R>0` for every parameter in (12), proving (1) throughout (11).

The formula also admits `a=1,r>0`: the old vertex `P2` then lies on the straight side `P3Q`, and the body is a nondegenerate triangle still with interior source. The same certificate remains strict. This optional boundary is not needed for the strict quadrilateral theorem.

Combining the three incidence regions proves the final scoped theorem:

> For the canonical centroided triangle and its three canonical balanced centroid cuts, adding any one actual ear that preserves the three old vertices as strict vertices produces a quadrilateral satisfying the strict cubic inequality (1). No bound on ear height, asymmetry, or cap fractions is required.

After an affine change applied simultaneously to body, source and cuts, this holds for an arbitrary triangle with its centroid cuts parallel to the opposite sides. In the actual diagonal family `Q(t)=P3+t(a,b)` with `a,b>0`, the full strict-convex ear interval is simply `t>3/(a+b)`; (11) follows automatically and the new proof handles the possible transitions through one or both cut rays. This does not imply a corresponding statement for arbitrary source/cut configurations on the starting triangle.
